name: Avakaya
subtitle: the raw mango pickle Andhra households measure the year by

ingredients.qty: 1kg, firm and sour, cut into 3cm pieces with the shell of the stone
ingredients.note: the stone shell is traditional and holds the pieces together
a coarse, deep red pickle chilli, not the fine hot kind
avakaya means mustard; this is the flavour
iodised salt clouds the pickle and softens the fruit
Indian gingelly oil, and enough to cover

prepNotes: Everything must be bone dry. One drop of water and the jar spoils within a week.
This is not a same-day pickle. It needs three days to come together and is better after a month.

steps.text: Wipe the mango pieces with a dry cloth and spread them on a towel for an hour. There must be no moisture at all.
steps.tip: Do not wash and use immediately. Wash the whole fruit, dry it thoroughly, then cut.

steps.text: Mix the chilli powder, ground mustard, salt, turmeric and fenugreek in a wide dry bowl.
Add half the oil and work it into a thick paste. Fold in the mango pieces and the garlic until every piece is coated.
Pack into a dry glass or ceramic jar, pressing down to remove air pockets. Pour the remaining oil over so the surface is covered.
steps.tip: The oil layer is the seal. If the pickle drinks it, top it up.

steps.text: Close and leave three days at room temperature, turning the jar once a day, then refrigerate.
steps.tip: Three days is the traditional cure. After that keep it cold: a jar left out all summer is a tradition, not a tested method.

storage: Keeps 6 months refrigerated under a covering film of oil, using only a dry spoon. Traditionally kept in a cool larder for a year, but that rests on the salt and oil levels being judged by eye, which is not something this recipe can verify for your batch.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
